title: The Thief and His Mother

full_text:
A young boy stole a hornbook from his schoolfellow and brought it home to his mother. Instead of correcting him, she praised his cleverness and patted his head. Encouraged by her approval, he stole a silver spoon from a neighbor, and she hid it with delight.

As the boy grew to manhood, his petty thefts expanded into violent highway robbery and murder. Eventually, he was captured by the king's soldiers and condemned to the gallows.

As he was led to the scaffold surrounded by a great crowd, his mother followed, weeping and tearing her hair. The condemned youth asked permission to whisper one last word in his mother's ear.

When she drew close, the youth clamped his teeth onto her earlobe and bit it clean off!

The crowd gasped in horror at the unnatural brutality. The youth turned to the crowd and cried with bitter tears: "Do not judge me alone! If this woman had struck my cheek when I first stole that little hornbook, I would not be standing beneath this gallows today; her praise has brought my ruin!"
moral: Neglecting to correct small faults in childhood breeds ruinous crimes in youth.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Thief and His Mother"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
